technical_and_design_decisions: Use Spring Framework 6.0 or later with Java 17+ for compatibility and modern features.
Integrate Apache Hadoop client libraries for HDFS sink implementation.
Leverage Spring Shell framework for adding Hadoop commands to the shell.
Design a repository pattern using Spring Data for composed job definitions to support flexible read/write operations.
Utilize Spring Cloud Data Flow concepts or a custom workflow engine for orchestrating composed jobs.
Implement module binding using Spring Expression Language (SpEL) or similar mechanisms for flexibility.
Ensure backward compatibility and minimal disruption during module migration from XD to s-c-s repositories.
assumptions: The existing codebase is based on the Spring ecosystem and is accessible for modification.
Required dependencies such as Hadoop client, Spring Shell, and Spring Data are available and can be integrated.
The developer has access to necessary development environments, tools, and test frameworks like JUnit.
No major architectural changes to the core system are needed; the increment focuses on adding modules and features.
Testing will be performed at unit, integration, and basic end-to-end levels without requiring complex infrastructure changes.

activities.activity_description: Analyze all user stories, understand requirements, and design high-level solutions and integration points for the software increment.
Develop the HDFS sink module, including integration with Hadoop libraries, configuration, and registration in the module registry.
Add support for Hadoop commands in the shell interface, enabling users to query the Hadoop file system.
Explore and design repository options for composed jobs, including prototyping and defining storage and access mechanisms.
Develop functionality to orchestrate composed jobs into workflows, allowing multiple jobs to be combined and operationalized.

activities.activity_name: Add Test Coverage for Shell Commands
activities.activity_description: Write unit and integration tests for shell commands to ensure isolation, coverage, and reduce reliance on end-to-end tests.
Add XD-like features for module binding using expressions or other mechanisms to bind message properties to microservice modules.
Move the JDBC module from the XD repository to the s-c-s repository, ensuring it functions as a sink in streaming pipelines.
Move the Kafka module from the XD repository to the s-c-s repository, adapting it for use as a source in streaming pipelines.
Perform integration testing across all new features, update documentation, and ensure the increment is ready for deployment.
